judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators at the same grain under the same Content Standard B4.1.1.2 'Demonstrate understanding of Roman numerals up XXX (30)' (Strand 1: Number, Sub-strand 1: Counting, Representation & Cardinality) with the same resolved coordinate BASIC 4 (rank 0), so direction rests on statement substance rather than rank. The second SFI (B4.1.1.2.1) establishes foundational understanding of the Roman numeral system up to XXX, with its single LC 'Develop an understanding of the Roman numeral system up to XXX (30)'. The first SFI (B4.1.1.2.2) applies that system operationally, with LCs 'Count in Roman numerals up to 30', 'Convert Hindu Arabic numerals to Roman numerals up to 30' and the reverse conversion, i.e. a substantive extension from system knowledge to counting and bidirectional conversion within the same 30 bound. Proficiency in reading/understanding the Roman numeral system supports success in counting and converting, so the developmental direction runs second_to_first. Source page/code proximity and token overlap alone were not treated as semantic evidence; bounded source evidence is truncated for both endpoints but the retained statement and LC text suffices for this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Content Standards in Strand 1: Number at the same canonical rank (2), but in different sub-strands: B6.1.1.3 covers factors, multiples and prime numbers from 1 to 100 (with HCF/LCM work visible in the bounded source context), while B6.1.4.1 covers the concept of ratios and its relationship to fractions and to multiplication and division of whole numbers. They share substantive multiplicative-structure coherence (common factors underpin simplifying and expressing equivalent ratios and fractions), which is more than token/code-prefix similarity. However, the shared tokens flagged by nomination are largely generic ('demonstrate', 'understanding', 'numbers'), no Learning Components are supplied, and both SFIs' source evidence is truncated, so the bounded evidence does not substantiate a same-rank developmental dependency in either direction; symmetric coherence is the supported judgment.
